desc:
Two very long strings are stored in run-length form. A string is given as a list of runs, each run [c, k] meaning the letter with code c (1 = a, 2 = b, ..., 26 = z) repeated k times; the string is the concatenation of all runs in order. Neighbouring runs may use the same letter, so the same string can be written in many different ways: [[1,2],[1,3]] and [[1,5]] both mean aaaaa.

Compare the two decoded strings in dictionary order and return -1 if a is smaller, 1 if a is larger and 0 if they are equal. A string that is a proper prefix of the other counts as smaller. The decoded strings can be far too long to build (the run counts go up to a billion).

Example: a = [[1,2],[2,1]] (aab) and b = [[1,1],[1,1],[3,1]] (aac) give -1.
constraints: each run is [c, k] with 1 ≤ c ≤ 26 and 1 ≤ k ≤ 1,000,000,000
the decoded strings may be much longer than 2<sup>31</sup>; do not build them
hints: Decoding both strings is impossible for counts near a billion. Compare run by run instead of letter by letter.
Walk through both lists with two pointers, each holding the current letter and how many copies of it are still unconsumed.

If the current letters differ, the answer is decided by them. Otherwise consume min(remaining_a, remaining_b) copies from both and move on when a run is used up. Whichever string ends first (with the other still having letters) is the smaller one.
editorial: Treat each list as a stream of letters, but consume it in bulk. Keep for each string the index of its current run and the number of copies left in it. While both streams have letters, compare the current letters: if they differ, the string with the smaller letter is smaller and we are done. If they are equal, remove t = min(left_a, left_b) copies from both; at least one run is exhausted, so we advance at least one pointer per step.

When one stream runs dry first, the other either also ends at that moment (equal strings, answer 0) or still has letters (the exhausted one is a proper prefix, so it is smaller). Adjacent runs with the same letter need no special treatment because we only ever compare current letters.

The loop performs at most |a| + |b| steps: O(|a| + |b|) time, O(1) extra space. Counts can sum to far more than 32 bits, so languages with fixed-width integers must keep the counts per run and never add them up.
